findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The 'fails without the fix part only' scope is written in the docs but the code does not enforce it. The revert command is added to the job-wide `ran` list, so it counts for every behavior criterion.
findings.evidence: verify.rs 365-382 builds one `ran` list, and the per-criterion check at 499-509 asks only whether each cited command is in `ran`. The plan pushes the revert record's command into that list, so any behavior criterion that cites the same text counts it as seen running. That includes the 'passes with the fix' part of a criterion whose only run was the failing run on the reverted tree. The plan's own Risk 1 and Open question admit this. Yet steps 1 and 11 would have the doc comment, the CHANGELOG and job-planning.md say the run counts 'for that part only', which the code does not do. The request asks for the count 'for the fails without the fix part', and the mechanism default asks that a rule be enforced or marked prose-only. The data to scope it exists: DemonstrationGroup.criteria (verify.rs 706-713) lists every criterion that names the command, and judge() walks criteria by index (line 470). Fix: Scope the rule to the criteria it demonstrates. Have revert_record carry the group's criterion numbers (for example a serde-default `criteria: Vec<u32>` beside `revert`, or one record per criterion). In judge(), use the record's command and name as seen running only when checking a criterion whose number is in that list, not by adding them to the job-wide `ran`. Add a criterion-3 case: a behavior criterion outside the group cites the revert command and stays unseen, with the Major finding. If the planner keeps the job-wide rule, the doc comment, CHANGELOG and job-planning.md must state the wider scope plainly and mark the 'that part only' limit as prose-only. Do not claim it.
findings.location: Plan step 4 (judge() revert rule), Decision 3, Open question, and step 11 (CHANGELOG / job-planning.md text)

findings.summary: The plan stores `passed: true` with exit code 101. This goes against the accepted reading, and it makes verification.json and the carried check lines misleading.
findings.evidence: The reading says the revert record's `passed` 'means the test failed as the criterion expected'. The plan sets passed = true always. Its reason is good: it avoids blocking the verdict, which keeps 64cb889's 'fails nothing' behavior. But a maintainer reading verification.json sees `passed: true, exit_code: 101`. The carried-check text the plan names (reading.rs 1880-1895, 'name: passed (exit code N)') would tell the next round 'fails-without-1: passed (exit code 101)'. Fix: Report the deviation from the reading in the change description. Have the revert record's doc comment say that `passed` means 'not a pass/fail check'. Either skip revert records in the carried lines (reading.rs) or render them as 'fails-without-1: revert run (exit code 101)', and test that.
findings.location: Decision 2 (passed = true) vs the accepted reading's 'Seen-running measurement' assumption; reading.rs 1880-1895 carried lines

findings.summary: close.rs is outside the listed deliverables, but the change is justified because it reads `verification.checks.len()`. Name it as a dependent in the change description.
findings.evidence: close.rs:631 uses `verification.checks.len()` as the 'N checks passed' count, so appending revert records changes that number. Athena's own finding flags the file as out of the deliverables. The edit is a needed follow-on of the record change, not scope creep. Fix: Keep the close.rs filter. Say in the change description why it is needed, and make step 7's test concrete: name the test and the expected count.

findings.summary: Criterion 3's cases pass on today's code, so they are regression guards for the new rule's limits, not tests that fail without the change.
findings.evidence: Before the change, a revert record with exit None or from another tree is already unseen (the filter at verify.rs 378 needs exit 0 or reused). The plan correctly says these tests fail only if the new rule drops its gates. Fix: Word it that way. Add the out-of-group case from the major finding, which is the one negative case the new rule can actually break.

summary: I checked the plan against the code: judge() in verify.rs (lines 362-382 and 470-520), DemonstrationGroup (verify.rs 706), demonstration_records in run/checks.rs (327-354), the check_runs order in run/verification.rs, and the readers of verification.checks (reading.rs 1584 and 1933, close.rs 631, introspect.rs, status.rs). The plan's structure holds up. A `revert` marker with serde default works, as does keeping the admission-searched filter line unchanged. Appending the records after the verifier's inputs are built shows nothing twice, and setting passed = true keeps blocking-check readers unaffected. The demonstrations use seams that exist: judge_recorded, run_demonstration_job and demo_seam. The dependents list matches what I found. The main problem is soundness: the revert command is added to the job-wide `ran` list. A behavior criterion's 'passes with the fix' part, or a different criterion that cites the same text, then counts as seen running on the strength of a failing run on the reverted tree. Meanwhile the docs and changelog would claim the rule covers 'that part only'. DemonstrationGroup.criteria already holds the data to scope the rule per criterion, so this can be fixed. The other findings are minor: passed = true goes against the reading and produces misleading carried text, and close.rs needs naming as a dependent. Verdict: revise.
